decls.name: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints
decls.doc:
The group homomorphism on points induced by a morphism of value algebras.

It sends an `A`-point `f : H →ₐ[R] A` to the `B`-point `φ ∘ f`.
decls.statement:
def mapPoints {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B) :
    points (H := H) A ⟶ points (H := H) B

decls.name: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints_apply
decls.doc: On points, `mapPoints` is post-composition with the algebra homomorphism `φ`.
decls.statement:
lemma mapPoints_apply {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B)
    (f : points (H := H) A) :
    mapPoints (H := H) φ f = toConv (φ.hom.comp f.ofConv)

decls.name: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints_one
decls.doc: The map on points sends the identity point to the identity point.
decls.statement:
lemma mapPoints_one {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B) :
    mapPoints (H := H) φ (1 : points (H := H) A) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints_mul
decls.doc: The map on points preserves multiplication of points.
decls.statement:
lemma mapPoints_mul {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B) (f g : points (H := H) A) :
    mapPoints (H := H) φ (f * g) = mapPoints (H := H) φ f * mapPoints (H := H) φ g

decls.name: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints_inv
decls.doc: The map on points preserves inverses of points.
decls.statement:
lemma mapPoints_inv {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B) (f : points (H := H) A) :
    mapPoints (H := H) φ f⁻¹ = (mapPoints (H := H) φ f)⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints_id
decls.doc: `mapPoints` preserves identity morphisms of value algebras.
decls.statement:
lemma mapPoints_id (A : CommAlgCat.{w} R) :
    mapPoints (H := H) (𝟙 A) = 𝟙 (points (H := H) A)

decls.name: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints_comp
decls.doc: `mapPoints` preserves composition of morphisms of value algebras.
decls.statement:
lemma mapPoints_comp {A B C : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B) (ψ : B ⟶ C) :
    mapPoints (H := H) (φ ≫ ψ) = mapPoints (H := H) φ ≫ mapPoints (H := H) ψ

decls.name: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.pointsFunctor
decls.doc:
The functor of points of the affine group object represented by a Hopf algebra.

It maps a commutative `R`-algebra `A` to the convolution group on algebra homomorphisms
`H →ₐ[R] A`, and maps `φ : A ⟶ B` to post-composition with `φ`.
decls.statement: def pointsFunctor : CommAlgCat.{w} R ⥤ GrpCat.{max v w}

decls.name: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.pointsFunctor_obj
decls.doc: The object part of `pointsFunctor` is the convolution group of algebra homomorphisms.
decls.statement:
lemma pointsFunctor_obj (A : CommAlgCat.{w} R) :
    (pointsFunctor (H := H)).obj A = GrpCat.of (WithConv (H →ₐ[R] A))

decls.name: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.pointsFunctor_map
decls.doc: The morphism part of `pointsFunctor` is post-composition in the value algebra.
decls.statement:
lemma pointsFunctor_map {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B) :
    (pointsFunctor (H := H)).map φ = mapPoints (H := H) φ

decls.name: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.pointsFunctor_map_apply_apply
decls.doc: The pointwise value of the image of an `A`-point under `pointsFunctor.map φ`.
decls.statement:
lemma pointsFunctor_map_apply_apply {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B)
    (f : WithConv (H →ₐ[R] A)) (h : H) :
    (((pointsFunctor (H := H)).map φ f : WithConv (H →ₐ[R] B)).ofConv) h =
      φ.hom (f.ofConv h)

decls.name: TauCeti.Algebra.TensorProduct.comp_productMap
decls.statement:
theorem comp_productMap (φ : A →ₐ[R] B) (f₁ : H₁ →ₐ[R] A) (f₂ : H₂ →ₐ[R] A) :
    φ.comp (_root_.Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap f₁ f₂) =
      _root_.Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap (φ.comp f₁) (φ.comp f₂)

decls.name: TauCeti.AffineGroup.Product.productMap_restrict
decls.doc:
A point of `Spec (H₁ ⊗[R] H₂)` is recovered from its two restrictions by Mathlib's
`Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap`.
decls.statement:
theorem productMap_restrict (g : (H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) →ₐ[R] A) :
    Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap (g.comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft)
        (g.comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight) =
      g

decls.name: TauCeti.AffineGroup.Product.restrictHom
decls.doc:
Restriction of a point of `Spec (H₁ ⊗[R] H₂)` to its two factors, as a monoid homomorphism
of convolution monoids: it pre-composes with the two inclusions `includeLeft` and
`includeRight`. Each component is `TauCeti.AlgHom.mapDomain` of a bialgebra morphism, hence a
monoid homomorphism, so their pairing is too.

decls.name: TauCeti.AffineGroup.Product.restrictHom_apply
decls.statement:
theorem restrictHom_apply (f : WithConv ((H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    restrictHom f = (AlgHom.mapDomain includeLeft f, AlgHom.mapDomain includeRight f)

decls.name: TauCeti.AffineGroup.Product.pointsMulEquiv
decls.doc:
The convolution monoid of `R`-algebra homomorphisms out of a tensor product of commutative
bialgebras `H₁ ⊗[R] H₂` is the product of the convolution monoids out of `H₁` and `H₂`.

On the functor of points this is the direct product of the affine group schemes `Spec H₁` and
`Spec H₂`: Mathlib's product map sends `x ⊗ₜ y` to `f₁ x * f₂ y`, and convolution is computed
componentwise. When `H₁` and `H₂` are Hopf algebras these convolution monoids are groups
(`TauCeti.AlgHom.instGroup`), so this is automatically an isomorphism of groups.
decls.statement:
def pointsMulEquiv :
    WithConv ((H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) →ₐ[R] A) ≃* WithConv (H₁ →ₐ[R] A) × WithConv (H₂ →ₐ[R] A)

decls.name: TauCeti.AffineGroup.Product.pointsMulEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_apply (f : WithConv ((H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMulEquiv f =
      (AlgHom.mapDomain includeLeft f, AlgHom.mapDomain includeRight f)

decls.name: TauCeti.AffineGroup.Product.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
    (p : WithConv (H₁ →ₐ[R] A) × WithConv (H₂ →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMulEquiv.symm p = toConv (Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap p.1.ofConv p.2.ofConv)

decls.name: TauCeti.AffineGroup.Product.restrictHom_mapValue
decls.doc:
Restricting a product point to the two factors commutes with post-composition in the value
algebra. This is the naturality square for the restriction homomorphism underlying
`pointsMulEquiv`.
decls.statement:
theorem restrictHom_mapValue (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (f : WithConv ((H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    restrictHom (AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) φ f) =
      (AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₁) φ (restrictHom f).1,
        AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₂) φ (restrictHom f).2)

decls.name: TauCeti.AffineGroup.Product.pointsMulEquiv_mapValue
decls.doc:
The product-points equivalence is natural in the value algebra.

Post-composing an `A`-valued point of `Spec (H₁ ⊗[R] H₂)` by `φ : A →ₐ[R] B`, then splitting
it into its two factor points, gives the same pair as first splitting and then post-composing
each factor point by `φ`.
decls.statement:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_mapValue (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (f : WithConv ((H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMulEquiv (A := B) (AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) φ f) =
      (AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₁) φ (pointsMulEquiv f).1,
        AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₂) φ (pointsMulEquiv f).2)

decls.name: TauCeti.AffineGroup.Product.pointsMulEquiv_mapValue_fst
decls.doc: First-component form of `pointsMulEquiv_mapValue`.
decls.statement:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_mapValue_fst (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (f : WithConv ((H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    (pointsMulEquiv (A := B) (AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) φ f)).1 =
      AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₁) φ (pointsMulEquiv f).1

decls.name: TauCeti.AffineGroup.Product.pointsMulEquiv_mapValue_snd
decls.doc: Second-component form of `pointsMulEquiv_mapValue`.
decls.statement:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_mapValue_snd (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (f : WithConv ((H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    (pointsMulEquiv (A := B) (AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) φ f)).2 =
      AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₂) φ (pointsMulEquiv f).2

decls.name: TauCeti.AffineGroup.Product.mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse product-points map is natural in the value algebra.

Assembling an `A`-valued product point from a pair of factor points and then post-composing by
`φ : A →ₐ[R] B` is the same as post-composing both factor points by `φ` and then assembling the
resulting `B`-valued product point.
decls.statement:
theorem mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (p : WithConv (H₁ →ₐ[R] A) × WithConv (H₂ →ₐ[R] A)) :
    AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) φ
        ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (H₁ := H₁) (H₂ := H₂) (A := A)).symm p) =
      (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (H₁ := H₁) (H₂ := H₂) (A := B)).symm
        (AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₁) φ p.1, AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₂) φ p.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.AffineGroup.Product.mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul
decls.doc:
On pure tensors, naturality of the inverse product-points map says that post-composition
by `φ` evaluates as applying `φ` to the product of the two factor values.
decls.statement:
theorem mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (p : WithConv (H₁ →ₐ[R] A) × WithConv (H₂ →ₐ[R] A)) (x : H₁) (y : H₂) :
    (AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₁ ⊗[R] H₂) φ
        ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (H₁ := H₁) (H₂ := H₂) (A := A)).symm p)).ofConv
        (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) =
      φ (p.1.ofConv x * p.2.ofConv y)

decls.name: TauCeti.AffineGroup.Product.pointsMulEquiv_symm_mapValue_apply_tmul
decls.doc:
On pure tensors, assembling after post-composing both factor points multiplies the two
post-composed factor values.
decls.statement:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_symm_mapValue_apply_tmul (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (p : WithConv (H₁ →ₐ[R] A) × WithConv (H₂ →ₐ[R] A)) (x : H₁) (y : H₂) :
    ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (H₁ := H₁) (H₂ := H₂) (A := B)).symm
        (AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₁) φ p.1, AlgHom.mapValue (H := H₂) φ p.2)).ofConv
        (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) =
      φ (p.1.ofConv x) * φ (p.2.ofConv y)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.baseChangePointsMulEquiv
decls.doc:
The `A`-points of the base change `K ⊗[k] k[Multiplicative (ZMod n)]` of `μ_n` are
the subgroup of `n`th roots of unity in `A`.

The source is the convolution group of `K`-algebra maps out of the base-changed Hopf algebra.
The target is Mathlib's subgroup of units whose `n`th power is one.

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.baseChangePointsMulEquiv_apply
decls.doc:
The base-changed roots-of-unity points equivalence reads a point by evaluating it on the
base-changed standard generator `1 ⊗ single (ofAdd 1) 1`.
decls.statement:
lemma baseChangePointsMulEquiv_apply (n : ℕ)
    (f : WithConv (K ⊗[k] MonoidAlgebra k (Multiplicative (ZMod n)) →ₐ[K] A)) :
    ((baseChangePointsMulEquiv (k := k) (K := K) (A := A) n f : Aˣ) : A) =
      f.ofConv (1 ⊗ₜ[k] MonoidAlgebra.single (generator n) (1 : k))

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul_single_generator
decls.doc:
The inverse base-changed roots-of-unity points equivalence evaluates scalar multiples of
the standard generator by scalar multiplication of the chosen root of unity.
decls.statement:
lemma baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul_single_generator (n : ℕ)
    (ζ : rootsOfUnity n A) (s : K) (r : k) :
    ((baseChangePointsMulEquiv (k := k) (K := K) (A := A) n).symm ζ).ofConv
        (s ⊗ₜ[k] MonoidAlgebra.single (generator n) r) =
      s • (r • ((ζ : Aˣ) : A))

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_generator
decls.doc:
The inverse base-changed roots-of-unity points equivalence takes the standard generator to
the chosen root of unity.
decls.statement:
lemma baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_generator (n : ℕ) (ζ : rootsOfUnity n A) :
    ((baseChangePointsMulEquiv (k := k) (K := K) (A := A) n).symm ζ).ofConv
        (1 ⊗ₜ[k] MonoidAlgebra.single (generator n) (1 : k)) =
      ((ζ : Aˣ) : A)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.generator
decls.doc: The standard generator of the character group defining `μ_n = D(ℤ/n)`.
decls.statement: abbrev generator (n : ℕ) : Multiplicative (ZMod n)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.characterMulEquivRootsOfUnity
decls.statement:
def characterMulEquivRootsOfUnity (n : ℕ) :
    (Multiplicative (ZMod n) →* Aˣ) ≃* rootsOfUnity n A

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.characterMulEquivRootsOfUnity_apply
decls.statement:
lemma characterMulEquivRootsOfUnity_apply (n : ℕ)
    (χ : Multiplicative (ZMod n) →* Aˣ) :
    ((characterMulEquivRootsOfUnity (A := A) n χ : Aˣ) : A) =
      (χ (generator n) : A)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.characterMulEquivRootsOfUnity_symm_apply_generator
decls.statement:
lemma characterMulEquivRootsOfUnity_symm_apply_generator
    (n : ℕ) (ζ : rootsOfUnity n A) :
    (((characterMulEquivRootsOfUnity (A := A) n).symm ζ (generator n) : Aˣ) : A) =
      ((ζ : Aˣ) : A)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.generator_pow_val
decls.statement:
lemma generator_pow_val (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (x : Multiplicative (ZMod n)) :
    generator n ^ (Multiplicative.toAdd x).val = x

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.pointsMulEquiv
decls.doc:
The functor of points of `μ_n = D(ℤ/n)` is the group of `n`th roots of unity.

The source is the convolution group of `R`-algebra maps out of the group algebra
`R[Multiplicative (ZMod n)]`, and the target is Mathlib's subgroup of units whose `n`th power
is one.

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.pointsMulEquiv_apply
decls.doc: The points equivalence sends a point to its value on the standard generator.
decls.statement:
lemma pointsMulEquiv_apply (n : ℕ)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n)) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) n f : Aˣ) : A) =
      f.ofConv (MonoidAlgebra.single (generator n) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.pointsMulEquiv_mapValue
decls.doc: The points equivalence is natural in the value algebra.
decls.statement:
lemma pointsMulEquiv_mapValue (n : ℕ) (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n)) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := B) n
        (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n))) φ f) =
      restrictRootsOfUnity φ.toMonoidHom n (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) n f)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_generator
decls.doc:
The inverse points equivalence sends a root of unity to the point taking the standard
generator to that root.
decls.statement:
lemma pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_generator (n : ℕ) (ζ : rootsOfUnity n A) :
    ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) n).symm ζ).ofConv
        (MonoidAlgebra.single (generator n) 1) =
      ((ζ : Aˣ) : A)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_generator_smul
decls.doc:
The inverse points equivalence evaluates scalar multiples of the standard generator by
scalar multiplication of the chosen root of unity.
decls.statement:
lemma pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_generator_smul (n : ℕ) (ζ : rootsOfUnity n A) (r : R) :
    ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) n).symm ζ).ofConv
        (MonoidAlgebra.single (generator n) r) =
      r • ((ζ : Aˣ) : A)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_zmod_val
decls.doc:
The inverse `μ_n` points equivalence evaluates the group-like generator indexed by
`x : Multiplicative (ZMod n)` as the corresponding power of the chosen root of unity.

For `x = generator n`, this specializes to
`RootsOfUnityGroup.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_generator`.
decls.statement:
lemma pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_zmod_val (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (ζ : rootsOfUnity n A)
    (x : Multiplicative (ZMod n)) :
    ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) n).symm ζ).ofConv
        (MonoidAlgebra.single x (1 : R)) =
      ((ζ : Aˣ) ^ (Multiplicative.toAdd x).val : Aˣ)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_zmod_val_smul
decls.doc:
The inverse `μ_n` points equivalence evaluates scalar multiples of the group-like generator
indexed by `x : Multiplicative (ZMod n)` by scalar multiplication of the corresponding power
of the chosen root of unity.
decls.statement:
lemma pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_zmod_val_smul (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (ζ : rootsOfUnity n A)
    (x : Multiplicative (ZMod n)) (r : R) :
    ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) n).symm ζ).ofConv
        (MonoidAlgebra.single x r) =
      r • (((ζ : Aˣ) ^ (Multiplicative.toAdd x).val : Aˣ) : A)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_ofAdd_val
decls.doc: The previous normal form, specialized to an additive residue class `j : ZMod n`.
decls.statement:
lemma pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_ofAdd_val (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (ζ : rootsOfUnity n A)
    (j : ZMod n) :
    ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) n).symm ζ).ofConv
        (MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd j) (1 : R)) =
      ((ζ : Aˣ) ^ j.val : Aˣ)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_ofAdd_val_smul
decls.doc: The scalar version of `pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_ofAdd_val`.
decls.statement:
lemma pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_ofAdd_val_smul (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (ζ : rootsOfUnity n A)
    (j : ZMod n) (r : R) :
    ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) n).symm ζ).ofConv
        (MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd j) r) =
      r • (((ζ : Aˣ) ^ j.val : Aˣ) : A)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc:
Naturality of the inverse `μ_n` points equivalence in the value algebra: post-composing
the point attached to `ζ` gives the point attached to the image of `ζ`.
decls.statement:
lemma mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (n : ℕ) (φ : A →ₐ[R] B) (ζ : rootsOfUnity n A) :
    AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n))) φ
        ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) n).symm ζ) =
      (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := B) n).symm
        (restrictRootsOfUnity φ.toMonoidHom n ζ)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_zmod_val
decls.doc:
Naturality of the inverse `μ_n` points equivalence, evaluated on an arbitrary cyclic
group-algebra generator.
decls.statement:
lemma mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_zmod_val (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (ζ : rootsOfUnity n A) (x : Multiplicative (ZMod n)) :
    (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n))) φ
        ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) n).symm ζ)).ofConv
        (MonoidAlgebra.single x (1 : R)) =
      φ (((ζ : Aˣ) ^ (Multiplicative.toAdd x).val : Aˣ) : A)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_zmod_val_smul
decls.doc:
Naturality of the inverse `μ_n` points equivalence on scalar multiples of arbitrary cyclic
group-algebra generators.
decls.statement:
lemma mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_zmod_val_smul (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (ζ : rootsOfUnity n A) (x : Multiplicative (ZMod n)) (r : R) :
    (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n))) φ
        ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) n).symm ζ)).ofConv
        (MonoidAlgebra.single x r) =
      φ (r • (((ζ : Aˣ) ^ (Multiplicative.toAdd x).val : Aˣ) : A))

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.toMultiplicativeZMod
decls.doc:
The quotient homomorphism `ℤ ↠ ℤ/n`, written multiplicatively as a homomorphism
`Multiplicative ℤ →* Multiplicative (ZMod n)`. Its diagonalizable image is the inclusion
`μ_n ↪ 𝔾ₘ`.
decls.statement: def toMultiplicativeZMod (n : ℕ) : Multiplicative ℤ →* Multiplicative (ZMod n)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.toMultiplicativeZMod_ofAdd
decls.doc: The multiplicative quotient sends `ofAdd k` to `ofAdd (k : ℤ/n)`.
decls.statement:
theorem toMultiplicativeZMod_ofAdd (n : ℕ) (k : ℤ) :
    toMultiplicativeZMod n (Multiplicative.ofAdd k) = Multiplicative.ofAdd (k : ZMod n)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.toMultiplicativeZMod_ofAdd_one
decls.doc:
The multiplicative quotient sends the `𝔾ₘ` generator `Multiplicative.ofAdd 1` to the
`μ_n` generator `Multiplicative.ofAdd 1`. This is not a `simp` lemma: `simp` already reduces
the left-hand side to `generator n` via `toMultiplicativeZMod_ofAdd` and `Int.cast_one`.
decls.statement:
theorem toMultiplicativeZMod_ofAdd_one (n : ℕ) :
    toMultiplicativeZMod n (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) = generator n

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.inclusion
decls.doc:
**The inclusion `μ_n ↪ 𝔾ₘ` on points.** It is the contravariant image of the quotient
`ℤ ↠ ℤ/n` under the diagonalizable functor: precomposition with the surjection
`R[Multiplicative ℤ] ↠ R[Multiplicative (ZMod n)]` of coordinate Hopf algebras carries a
point of `μ_n = D(ℤ/n)` to a point of `𝔾ₘ = D(ℤ)`.
decls.title: The inclusion `μ_n ↪ 𝔾ₘ` on points

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.inclusion_apply
decls.doc: The inclusion acts by precomposition with the diagonalizable image of the quotient.
decls.statement:
theorem inclusion_apply (n : ℕ)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n)) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    inclusion n f = DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMap (toMultiplicativeZMod n) f

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.charOfPoint_inclusion
decls.doc:
**Reading the character of an included point.** The character of `inclusion n f`, a point of
`𝔾ₘ`, is the `μ_n` character of `f` precomposed with the quotient `ℤ ↠ ℤ/n`.

This is the general reduction; it is not a `simp` lemma because it would rewrite the left-hand
side of the terminal evaluation lemma `charOfPoint_inclusion_ofAdd_one`, which is the useful
`simp` normal form.
decls.title: Reading the character of an included point
decls.statement:
theorem charOfPoint_inclusion (n : ℕ)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n)) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    DiagonalizableGroup.charOfPoint (inclusion n f).ofConv =
      (DiagonalizableGroup.charOfPoint f.ofConv).comp (toMultiplicativeZMod n)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.charOfPoint_inclusion_ofAdd_one
decls.doc:
**The inclusion is the inclusion of roots of unity.** Reading the included point
`inclusion n f`, a point of `𝔾ₘ`, on the `𝔾ₘ` group-algebra generator `Multiplicative.ofAdd 1`
returns the underlying unit of the root of unity `RootsOfUnityGroup.pointsMulEquiv n f`.
decls.title: The inclusion is the inclusion of roots of unity
decls.statement:
theorem charOfPoint_inclusion_ofAdd_one (n : ℕ)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n)) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    DiagonalizableGroup.charOfPoint (inclusion n f).ofConv (Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ℤ)) =
      (RootsOfUnityGroup.pointsMulEquiv n f : Aˣ)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.multiplicativeGroup_pointEquiv_inclusion
decls.doc:
The same identification against the canonical Laurent-polynomial `𝔾ₘ` of
`TauCeti.MultiplicativeGroup`: pushing the included point along
`AddMonoidAlgebra.toMultiplicativeAlgEquiv` and reading it with `MultiplicativeGroup.pointEquiv`
returns the underlying unit of the root of unity.
decls.statement:
theorem multiplicativeGroup_pointEquiv_inclusion (n : ℕ)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n)) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    Units.map (inclusion n f).ofConv
        (MultiplicativeGroup.unitOfPoint
          (AddMonoidAlgebra.toMultiplicativeAlgEquiv R ℤ).toAlgHom) =
      (RootsOfUnityGroup.pointsMulEquiv n f : Aˣ)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.toMultiplicativeZMod_surjective
decls.doc: The multiplicative quotient `ℤ ↠ ℤ/n` is surjective.
decls.statement: theorem toMultiplicativeZMod_surjective (n : ℕ) : Function.Surjective (toMultiplicativeZMod n)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.inclusion_injective
decls.doc:
**The inclusion is a monomorphism of functors.** The quotient `ℤ ↠ ℤ/n` is surjective, so
precomposing characters with it is injective; since a point is determined by its character, the
induced points homomorphism `μ_n(A) → 𝔾ₘ(A)` is injective.
decls.title: The inclusion is a monomorphism of functors
decls.statement:
theorem inclusion_injective (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (inclusion (R := R) (A := A) n)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.mapValue_inclusion
decls.doc:
**Naturality in the value algebra.** The inclusion `μ_n → 𝔾ₘ` commutes with the
value-algebra functoriality `AlgHom.mapValue`.
decls.title: Naturality in the value algebra
decls.statement:
theorem mapValue_inclusion (n : ℕ) (φ : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    (inclusion (R := R) (A := B) n).comp
        (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n))) φ) =
      (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ)) φ).comp
        (inclusion (R := R) (A := A) n)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.powEnd_comp_inclusion
decls.doc:
**The `n`th power endomorphism of `𝔾ₘ` annihilates `μ_n`.** Composing the power endomorphism
`DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd n` after the inclusion `μ_n ↪ 𝔾ₘ` is the trivial homomorphism of
group functors: every `μ_n`-point maps to a root of unity, whose `n`th power is `1`.
decls.title: The `n`th power endomorphism of `𝔾ₘ` annihilates `μ_n`
decls.statement:
theorem powEnd_comp_inclusion (n : ℕ) :
    (DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd (R := R) (A := A) (n : ℤ)).comp (inclusion n) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.powEnd_inclusion
decls.doc:
The `n`th power endomorphism annihilates every `μ_n`-point, in element form. This is not a
`simp` lemma: when the power-endomorphism API is also imported,
`DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd_apply` rewrites the left-hand side to `inclusion n f ^ n`, so the
statement below is never in `simp`-normal form in that import context.
decls.statement:
theorem powEnd_inclusion (n : ℕ)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n)) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd (R := R) (A := A) (n : ℤ) (inclusion n f) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.mem_range_inclusion
decls.doc:
**A `𝔾ₘ`-point killed by the `n`th power lies in the image of `μ_n`.** If the `n`th power
endomorphism sends `g` to the identity, then `g` reads off a unit `u` with `u ^ n = 1`, i.e. an
`n`th root of unity, and `g` is the image of the `μ_n`-point attached to it.
decls.title: A `𝔾ₘ`-point killed by the `n`th power lies in the image of `μ_n`
decls.statement:
theorem mem_range_inclusion (n : ℕ)
    {g : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A)}
    (hg : DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd (R := R) (A := A) (n : ℤ) g = 1) :
    g ∈ MonoidHom.range (G := WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n)) →ₐ[R] A))
      (N := WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A))
      (inclusion (R := R) (A := A) n)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.mem_range_inclusion_iff
decls.doc:
**Membership in the image of `μ_n ↪ 𝔾ₘ`.** A `𝔾ₘ`-point lies in the image of the `μ_n`
inclusion exactly when the `n`th power endomorphism kills it: `g` comes from `μ_n` iff `gⁿ = 1`.
decls.title: Membership in the image of `μ_n ↪ 𝔾ₘ`
decls.statement:
theorem mem_range_inclusion_iff (n : ℕ)
    {g : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A)} :
    g ∈ MonoidHom.range (G := WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n)) →ₐ[R] A))
        (N := WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A))
        (inclusion (R := R) (A := A) n) ↔
      DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd (R := R) (A := A) (n : ℤ) g = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.RootsOfUnityGroup.range_inclusion
decls.doc:
**`μ_n` is the kernel of the `n`th power endomorphism of `𝔾ₘ`.** As subgroups of the group of
`𝔾ₘ`-points, the image of the inclusion `μ_n ↪ 𝔾ₘ` equals the kernel of the `n`th power
endomorphism `DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd n`: a `𝔾ₘ`-point comes from `μ_n` exactly when its `n`th
power is trivial. This realizes `μ_n = ker(𝔾ₘ --u ↦ uⁿ--> 𝔾ₘ)` on the functor of points.
decls.title: `μ_n` is the kernel of the `n`th power endomorphism of `𝔾ₘ`
decls.statement:
theorem range_inclusion (n : ℕ) :
    MonoidHom.range (G := WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (ZMod n)) →ₐ[R] A))
        (N := WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A))
        (inclusion (R := R) (A := A) n) =
      MonoidHom.ker (G := WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A))
        (M := WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A))
        (DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd (R := R) (A := A) (n : ℤ))

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.baseChangePointsMulEquiv
decls.doc:
The `A`-points of the base change of the rank-`σ` split torus are coordinate families
`σ → Aˣ`.

The source is the convolution group of `K`-algebra maps out of the base-changed Hopf algebra
`K ⊗[k] k[Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)]`; the target is the product group of units of the value
algebra.
decls.statement:
def baseChangePointsMulEquiv :
    WithConv (K ⊗[k] MonoidAlgebra k (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)) →ₐ[K] A) ≃* (σ → Aˣ)

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.baseChangePointsMulEquiv_apply_coe
decls.doc:
The base-changed split-torus points equivalence reads a point by evaluating it on the
base-changed standard coordinate generator indexed by `i`.
decls.statement:
theorem baseChangePointsMulEquiv_apply_coe
    (f : WithConv (K ⊗[k] MonoidAlgebra k (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)) →ₐ[K] A))
    (i : σ) :
    (baseChangePointsMulEquiv f i : A) =
      f.ofConv (1 ⊗ₜ[k]
        MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd (Finsupp.single i 1)) (1 : k))

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul_single
decls.doc:
The inverse base-changed split-torus points equivalence sends a pure tensor
`s ⊗ single (ofAdd m) r` to the scalar multiple of the monomial in the chosen coordinates
with exponent vector `m`.
decls.statement:
theorem baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul_single (c : σ → Aˣ) (s : K)
    (m : σ →₀ ℤ) (r : k) :
    ((baseChangePointsMulEquiv (k := k) (K := K) (A := A) (σ := σ)).symm c).ofConv
        (s ⊗ₜ[k] MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd m) r) =
      s • (r • ((m.prod fun i n => c i ^ n : Aˣ) : A))

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_one
decls.doc:
The inverse base-changed split-torus points equivalence takes the standard coordinate
generator indexed by `i` to the chosen coordinate `c i`.
decls.statement:
theorem baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_one (c : σ → Aˣ) (i : σ) :
    ((baseChangePointsMulEquiv (k := k) (K := K) (A := A) (σ := σ)).symm c).ofConv
        (1 ⊗ₜ[k] MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd (Finsupp.single i 1)) (1 : k)) =
      (c i : A)

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pointsMulEquiv
decls.doc:
The functor of points of the rank-`σ` split torus `D(Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ))`: for every
commutative `R`-algebra `A`, the convolution group of `R`-algebra maps out of
`R[Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)]` is the product group `σ → Aˣ`, under pointwise multiplication.
decls.statement:
def pointsMulEquiv :
    WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)) →ₐ[R] A) ≃* (σ → Aˣ)

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pointsMulEquiv_apply_coe
decls.doc:
The points equivalence reads off the value of a point on the `i`-th standard generator
`single (ofAdd (single i 1)) 1` of `R[Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)]`.
decls.statement:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_apply_coe
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)) →ₐ[R] A)) (i : σ) :
    (pointsMulEquiv f i : A) =
      f.ofConv (MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd (Finsupp.single i 1)) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse points equivalence sends a family `c : σ → Aˣ` to the point extending the
character of `Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)` determined by `c`.
decls.statement:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (c : σ → Aˣ) :
    (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A)).symm c =
      toConv (DiagonalizableGroup.point (freeAbelianCharEquiv.symm c))

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single
decls.doc:
The inverse points equivalence sends a coordinate family to the point taking the `i`-th
standard generator to the `i`-th coordinate.
decls.statement:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single (c : σ → Aˣ) (i : σ) :
    ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A)).symm c).ofConv
        (MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd (Finsupp.single i 1)) 1) =
      (c i : A)

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pointsMulEquiv_mapValue
decls.doc:
The split-torus points equivalence is natural in the value algebra: post-composing a point
with an `R`-algebra map `φ : A →ₐ[R] B` sends each coordinate through the induced map on
units.
decls.statement:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_mapValue (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)) →ₐ[R] A)) (i : σ) :
    pointsMulEquiv (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ))) φ f) i =
      Units.map φ.toMonoidHom (pointsMulEquiv f i)

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc: Naturality of the inverse split-torus points equivalence in the value algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (φ : A →ₐ[R] B) (c : σ → Aˣ) :
    AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ))) φ
        ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A)).symm c) =
      (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := B)).symm
        (fun i => Units.map φ.toMonoidHom (c i))

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.cocharEquiv
decls.doc:
The **cocharacter lattice `X_*(T)`** of the rank-`σ` split torus
`T = D(Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ))`, identified with `σ → ℤ`. A cocharacter
`ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ` is read off on the standard generators
`ofAdd (single i 1)`, its coordinate at `i` being `(ψ (ofAdd (single i 1))).toAdd`. This is
`TauCeti.freeAbelianCharEquiv` (with target `Multiplicative ℤ`) followed by `Multiplicative.toAdd`
in each coordinate.
decls.statement:
def cocharEquiv :
    (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) ≃ (σ → ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.cocharEquiv_apply
decls.doc:
The `i`-th coordinate of a cocharacter is its value on the standard generator
`ofAdd (single i 1)`, read as an integer through `Multiplicative.toAdd`.
decls.statement:
theorem cocharEquiv_apply (ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) (i : σ) :
    cocharEquiv ψ i = (ψ (Multiplicative.ofAdd (Finsupp.single i 1))).toAdd

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.cocharEquiv_one
decls.doc:
Reading off cocharacter coordinates is additive: the trivial cocharacter has zero
coordinates.
decls.statement: theorem cocharEquiv_one : cocharEquiv (1 : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.cocharEquiv_mul
decls.doc:
Reading off cocharacter coordinates is additive: the product of cocharacters (the group
operation on the cocharacter lattice) corresponds to pointwise addition of coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem cocharEquiv_mul (ψ φ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) :
    cocharEquiv (ψ * φ) = cocharEquiv ψ + cocharEquiv φ

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.cocharAddEquiv
decls.doc:
The **cocharacter lattice `X_*(T)`** as a `ℤ`-module, bundled: the additive form of
`cocharEquiv`, identifying `Additive (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ)` (the
cocharacter group with its natural additive structure) with `σ → ℤ` as an `AddEquiv`. This
carries the algebraic compatibility that `cocharEquiv` reads off pointwise (`cocharEquiv_one`,
`cocharEquiv_mul`), so it transports the natural `ℤ`-module structure.
decls.statement:
def cocharAddEquiv :
    Additive (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) ≃+ (σ → ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.cocharAddEquiv_apply
decls.doc: `cocharAddEquiv` agrees coordinatewise with the unbundled `cocharEquiv`.
decls.statement:
theorem cocharAddEquiv_apply (ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) (i : σ) :
    cocharAddEquiv (Additive.ofMul ψ) i = cocharEquiv ψ i

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pairing_ofAdd_eq
decls.doc:
**The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing is the dot product.** For a character
`ofAdd m` of `T` (`m : σ →₀ ℤ = X*(T)`) and a cocharacter `ψ` (with coordinates
`cocharEquiv ψ : σ → ℤ = X_*(T)`), the pairing `⟨ofAdd m, ψ⟩` of
`TauCeti.Algebra.AlgebraicGroup.Cocharacter` is `∑ᵢ mᵢ · cocharEquiv ψ i`. This is the
canonical evaluation pairing between the free `ℤ`-module `σ →₀ ℤ` and its dual `σ → ℤ`,
extending the rank-`1` `DiagonalizableGroup.pairing_ofAdd` to arbitrary rank.
decls.title: The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing is the dot product
decls.statement:
theorem pairing_ofAdd_eq (ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) (m : σ →₀ ℤ) :
    DiagonalizableGroup.pairing (Multiplicative.ofAdd m) ψ =
      m.sum fun i c => c * cocharEquiv ψ i

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.dotPairing
decls.doc:
**The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing as a `ℤ`-bilinear map.** On the character
lattice `X*(T) = σ →₀ ℤ` and the cocharacter lattice `X_*(T) = σ → ℤ` (via `cocharEquiv`) the
pairing is the evaluation/dot product `⟨m, v⟩ = ∑ᵢ mᵢ vᵢ`, packaged from Mathlib's
`Finsupp.llift`. It agrees with the character–cocharacter pairing of
`TauCeti.Algebra.AlgebraicGroup.Cocharacter` through `cocharEquiv` (`pairing_eq_dotPairing`).
decls.title: The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing as a `ℤ`-bilinear map
decls.statement: def dotPairing : (σ →₀ ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] (σ → ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.dotPairing_apply
decls.statement:
theorem dotPairing_apply (m : σ →₀ ℤ) (v : σ → ℤ) :
    dotPairing m v = m.sum fun i c => c * v i

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pairing_eq_dotPairing
decls.doc:
**The dot-product pairing computes the character–cocharacter pairing.** For a character
`ofAdd m` and a cocharacter `ψ` (with coordinates `cocharEquiv ψ`), the pairing
`⟨ofAdd m, ψ⟩` of `TauCeti.Algebra.AlgebraicGroup.Cocharacter` is `dotPairing m (cocharEquiv ψ)`.
decls.title: The dot-product pairing computes the character–cocharacter pairing
decls.statement:
theorem pairing_eq_dotPairing (ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) (m : σ →₀ ℤ) :
    DiagonalizableGroup.pairing (Multiplicative.ofAdd m) ψ = dotPairing m (cocharEquiv ψ)

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.instIsPerfPair
decls.doc:
**The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing is perfect (finite rank).** For a
finite-rank split torus (`Finite σ`), the dot-product pairing `dotPairing` between the character
lattice `X*(T) = σ →₀ ℤ` and the cocharacter lattice `X_*(T) = σ → ℤ` is a perfect pairing in the
sense of Mathlib's `LinearMap.IsPerfPair`: both induced maps to the `ℤ`-duals are isomorphisms.
This is the split-torus perfect pairing that is the input to root data. (For arbitrary `σ` the
pairing stays non-degenerate in each slot — `eq_zero_of_forall_pairing_eq_zero`,
`eq_one_of_forall_pairing_eq_zero` — while perfectness is proved only in finite rank.)
decls.title: The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing is perfect (finite rank)
decls.statement: instance instIsPerfPair [Finite σ] : (dotPairing (σ := σ)).IsPerfPair

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.latticePairing
decls.doc:
**The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing on the genuine lattices.** The dot-product
pairing `dotPairing`, with its coordinate model `σ → ℤ` of the cocharacter lattice transported
back along `cocharAddEquiv` to the genuine cocharacter lattice
`X_*(T) = Additive (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ)`. On a cocharacter `ψ` it is
still `⟨ofAdd m, ψ⟩ = ∑ᵢ mᵢ · cocharEquiv ψ i` (`latticePairing_ofMul`).
decls.title: The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing on the genuine lattices

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.latticePairing_ofMul
decls.doc:
`latticePairing` evaluated on a cocharacter is the character–cocharacter pairing, the dot
product `⟨ofAdd m, ψ⟩ = ∑ᵢ mᵢ · cocharEquiv ψ i`.
decls.statement:
theorem latticePairing_ofMul (m : σ →₀ ℤ)
    (ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) :
    latticePairing m (Additive.ofMul ψ) =
      DiagonalizableGroup.pairing (Multiplicative.ofAdd m) ψ

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.instLatticePairingIsPerfPair
decls.doc:
**The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing is perfect (finite rank), on the genuine
cocharacter lattice.** For a finite-rank split torus (`Finite σ`), `latticePairing` between the
character lattice `X*(T) = σ →₀ ℤ` and the genuine cocharacter lattice
`X_*(T) = Additive (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ)` is a perfect pairing in the
sense of Mathlib's `LinearMap.IsPerfPair`, transported from `instIsPerfPair` along
`cocharAddEquiv`.
decls.statement: instance instLatticePairingIsPerfPair [Finite σ] : (latticePairing (σ := σ)).IsPerfPair

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.charPoints_comp_cocharPoints_ofAdd
decls.doc:
**The dot-product pairing is realized on points as a power endomorphism of `𝔾ₘ`.**
Composing the character `ofAdd m` after the cocharacter `ψ` is the power endomorphism of `𝔾ₘ`
with exponent the dot product `∑ᵢ mᵢ · cocharEquiv ψ i`, so on points it raises a unit to that
power. This is the split-torus instance of `DiagonalizableGroup.charPoints_comp_cocharPoints`.
decls.title: The dot-product pairing is realized on points as a power endomorphism of `𝔾ₘ`
decls.statement:
theorem charPoints_comp_cocharPoints_ofAdd
    (m : σ →₀ ℤ) (ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) :
    (DiagonalizableGroup.charPoints (R := R) (A := A) (Multiplicative.ofAdd m)).comp
        (DiagonalizableGroup.cocharPoints ψ) =
      DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd (m.sum fun i c => c * cocharEquiv ψ i)

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.eq_zero_of_forall_pairing_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**Left non-degeneracy of the split-torus pairing.** A character `ofAdd m` pairing to `0`
against every cocharacter is trivial: `m = 0`. This holds for arbitrary `σ`; for finite `σ` the
pairing is moreover perfect (`instIsPerfPair`).
decls.title: Left non-degeneracy of the split-torus pairing
decls.statement:
theorem eq_zero_of_forall_pairing_eq_zero {m : σ →₀ ℤ}
    (h : ∀ ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ,
      DiagonalizableGroup.pairing (Multiplicative.ofAdd m) ψ = 0) :
    m = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.SplitTorus.eq_one_of_forall_pairing_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**Right non-degeneracy of the split-torus pairing.** A cocharacter `ψ` pairing to `0`
against every character is trivial: `ψ = 1`. This holds for arbitrary `σ`; for finite `σ` the
pairing is moreover perfect (`instIsPerfPair`).
decls.title: Right non-degeneracy of the split-torus pairing

decls.name: TauCeti.TrivialGroup.pointsMulEquiv
decls.doc:
The functor of points of the trivial affine group is the one-element group.

The source is the convolution group of `R`-algebra maps out of the Hopf algebra `R`; since
there is only one such algebra map, the convolution group is multiplicatively equivalent to
`PUnit`.
decls.statement: def pointsMulEquiv : WithConv (R →ₐ[R] A) ≃* PUnit.{1}

decls.name: TauCeti.TrivialGroup.pointsMulEquiv_apply
decls.doc: The equivalence sends every convolution point to the unique element of `PUnit`.
decls.statement:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_apply (f : WithConv (R →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) f = PUnit.unit

decls.name: TauCeti.TrivialGroup.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc: The inverse equivalence sends the unique element of `PUnit` to `Algebra.ofId R A`.
decls.statement:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (u : PUnit.{1}) :
    (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A)).symm u = toConv (Algebra.ofId R A)

decls.name: TauCeti.TrivialGroup.convPoint_eq_one
decls.doc: The unique convolution point is the identity point.
decls.statement: theorem convPoint_eq_one (f : WithConv (R →ₐ[R] A)) : f = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.TrivialGroup.convPoint_eq_one_iff
decls.doc: The identity normal form for trivial-group convolution points, as a simp proposition.
decls.statement: theorem convPoint_eq_one_iff (f : WithConv (R →ₐ[R] A)) : f = 1 ↔ True

decls.name: TauCeti.TrivialGroup.ofConv_eq_ofId
decls.doc: The underlying algebra map of any trivial-group convolution point is `Algebra.ofId`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofConv_eq_ofId (f : WithConv (R →ₐ[R] A)) :
    f.ofConv = Algebra.ofId R A

decls.name: TauCeti.TrivialGroup.convPoint_apply
decls.doc: Evaluating any trivial-group convolution point gives the algebra map.
decls.statement:
theorem convPoint_apply (f : WithConv (R →ₐ[R] A)) (r : R) :
    f r = algebraMap R A r

decls.name: TauCeti.TrivialGroup.toConv_eq_one
decls.doc: Every `R`-algebra map `R →ₐ[R] A` becomes the convolution identity.
decls.statement: theorem toConv_eq_one (f : R →ₐ[R] A) : toConv f = (1 : WithConv (R →ₐ[R] A))

decls.name: TauCeti.TrivialGroup.convInv_apply
decls.doc: Evaluating the inverse of a trivial-group point gives the algebra map.
decls.statement:
theorem convInv_apply (f : WithConv (R →ₐ[R] A)) (r : R) :
    f⁻¹ r = algebraMap R A r

decls.name: TauCeti.TrivialGroup.pointsMulEquiv_mapValue
decls.doc: The trivial-group points equivalence is natural in the value algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_mapValue (φ : A →ₐ[R] B) (f : WithConv (R →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := B)
        (AlgHom.mapValue (H := R) φ f) =
      pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) f

decls.name: TauCeti.TrivialGroup.mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc: Naturality of the inverse trivial-group points equivalence in the value algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (φ : A →ₐ[R] B) (u : PUnit.{1}) :
    AlgHom.mapValue (H := R) φ ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A)).symm u) =
      (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := B)).symm u

decls.name: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.prodGroupLike
decls.doc:
The group-like monoid homomorphism `(g, h) ↦ single g 1 ⊗ₜ single h 1` from `G × H` into the
multiplicative monoid of `R[G] ⊗[R] R[H]`.
decls.statement:
def prodGroupLike :
    G × H →* MonoidAlgebra R G ⊗[R] MonoidAlgebra R H

decls.name: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.prodGroupLike_apply
decls.statement:
theorem prodGroupLike_apply (g : G) (h : H) :
    prodGroupLike R (g, h) = single g (1 : R) ⊗ₜ[R] single h 1

decls.name: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.prodTensorAlgHom
decls.doc:
The forward algebra map `R[G × H] →ₐ[R] R[G] ⊗[R] R[H]`, sending `single (g, h) 1` to
`single g 1 ⊗ₜ single h 1`.
decls.statement:
def prodTensorAlgHom :
    MonoidAlgebra R (G × H) →ₐ[R] MonoidAlgebra R G ⊗[R] MonoidAlgebra R H

decls.name: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.prodTensorAlgHom_single
decls.statement:
theorem prodTensorAlgHom_single (g : G) (h : H) :
    prodTensorAlgHom R (single (g, h) (1 : R)) = single g 1 ⊗ₜ[R] single h 1

decls.name: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.commute_mapDomainAlgHom_inl_inr
decls.doc: The images of the two inclusions `R[G] → R[G × H]` and `R[H] → R[G × H]` commute.
decls.statement:
theorem commute_mapDomainAlgHom_inl_inr (x : MonoidAlgebra R G) (y : MonoidAlgebra R H) :
    Commute (mapDomainAlgHom R R (MonoidHom.inl G H) x)
      (mapDomainAlgHom R R (MonoidHom.inr G H) y)

decls.name: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.tensorProdAlgHom
decls.doc:
The inverse algebra map `R[G] ⊗[R] R[H] →ₐ[R] R[G × H]`, the tensor-product universal map of
the two inclusions `R[G] → R[G × H]` and `R[H] → R[G × H]`.
decls.statement:
def tensorProdAlgHom :
    MonoidAlgebra R G ⊗[R] MonoidAlgebra R H →ₐ[R] MonoidAlgebra R (G × H)

decls.name: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.tensorProdAlgHom_tmul_single
decls.statement:
theorem tensorProdAlgHom_tmul_single (g : G) (h : H) :
    tensorProdAlgHom R (single g (1 : R) ⊗ₜ[R] single h 1) = single (g, h) 1

decls.name: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.prodTensorAlgEquiv
decls.statement:
def prodTensorAlgEquiv :
    MonoidAlgebra R (G × H) ≃ₐ[R] MonoidAlgebra R G ⊗[R] MonoidAlgebra R H

decls.name: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.prodTensorAlgEquiv_single
decls.statement:
theorem prodTensorAlgEquiv_single (g : G) (h : H) :
    prodTensorAlgEquiv R (single (g, h) (1 : R)) = single g 1 ⊗ₜ[R] single h 1

decls.name: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.prodTensorAlgEquiv_symm_tmul_single
decls.statement:
theorem prodTensorAlgEquiv_symm_tmul_single (g : G) (h : H) :
    (prodTensorAlgEquiv R).symm (single g (1 : R) ⊗ₜ[R] single h 1) = single (g, h) 1

decls.name: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.prodTensorBialgEquiv
decls.doc:
**The monoid algebra of a product is the tensor product of monoid algebras**, as a bialgebra
isomorphism.
decls.title: The monoid algebra of a product is the tensor product of monoid algebras
decls.statement:
def prodTensorBialgEquiv :
    MonoidAlgebra R (G × H) ≃ₐc[R] MonoidAlgebra R G ⊗[R] MonoidAlgebra R H

decls.name: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.prodTensorBialgEquiv_single
decls.doc:
The forward product bialgebra equivalence sends the generator indexed by `(g, h)` to the
pure tensor of the two factor generators.
decls.statement:
theorem prodTensorBialgEquiv_single (g : G) (h : H) :
    prodTensorBialgEquiv R (single (g, h) (1 : R)) = single g 1 ⊗ₜ[R] single h 1

decls.name: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.prodTensorBialgEquiv_symm_tmul_single
decls.doc:
The inverse product bialgebra equivalence sends a pure tensor of factor generators to the
generator indexed by their product pair.
decls.statement:
theorem prodTensorBialgEquiv_symm_tmul_single (g : G) (h : H) :
    (prodTensorBialgEquiv R).symm (single g (1 : R) ⊗ₜ[R] single h 1) = single (g, h) 1

decls.name: Bialgebra.Quotient.liftBialgHom_kill
decls.statement:
theorem liftBialgHom_kill (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : J ≤ RingHom.ker f.toAlgHom.toRingHom) {h : H} (hh : h ∈ J) :
    (f : H →ₐ[R] K) h = 0

decls.name: Bialgebra.Quotient.liftBialgHomAlg
decls.statement:
abbrev liftBialgHomAlg (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : J ≤ RingHom.ker f.toAlgHom.toRingHom) : H ⧸ J →ₐ[R] K

decls.name: Bialgebra.Quotient.liftBialgHomAlg_mk
decls.statement:
theorem liftBialgHomAlg_mk (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : J ≤ RingHom.ker f.toAlgHom.toRingHom) (h : H) :
    liftBialgHomAlg J f hf (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R J h) = f h

decls.name: Bialgebra.Quotient.liftBialgHomAlg_toLinearMap_comp_mkₐ
decls.statement:
theorem liftBialgHomAlg_toLinearMap_comp_mkₐ (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : J ≤ RingHom.ker f.toAlgHom.toRingHom) :
    (liftBialgHomAlg J f hf).toLinearMap.comp
      (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R J).toLinearMap = f.toLinearMap

decls.name: Bialgebra.Quotient.liftBialgHomAlg_comul_mk
decls.statement:
theorem liftBialgHomAlg_comul_mk (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : J ≤ RingHom.ker f.toAlgHom.toRingHom) (h : H) :
    _root_.TensorProduct.map (liftBialgHomAlg J f hf).toLinearMap
        (liftBialgHomAlg J f hf).toLinearMap
        (_root_.TensorProduct.map (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R J).toLinearMap
          (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R J).toLinearMap (Coalgebra.comul h)) =
      Coalgebra.comul (R := R) (f h)

decls.name: Bialgebra.Quotient.liftBialgHom
decls.doc:
A bialgebra morphism out of `H` which kills a two-sided coideal `J` factors through the
quotient bialgebra `H ⧸ J`.
decls.statement:
def liftBialgHom (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : J ≤ RingHom.ker f.toAlgHom.toRingHom) : H ⧸ J →ₐc[R] K

decls.name: Bialgebra.Quotient.liftBialgHom_mk
decls.doc: The quotient lift, evaluated on a quotient class.
decls.statement:
theorem liftBialgHom_mk (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : J ≤ RingHom.ker f.toAlgHom.toRingHom) (h : H) :
    liftBialgHom J f hf (Ideal.Quotient.mk J h) = f h

decls.name: Bialgebra.Quotient.liftBialgHom_comp_mkBialgHom
decls.doc: The quotient lift composed with the quotient map is the original bialgebra morphism.
decls.statement:
theorem liftBialgHom_comp_mkBialgHom (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : J ≤ RingHom.ker f.toAlgHom.toRingHom) :
    (liftBialgHom J f hf).comp (Bialgebra.Quotient.mkBialgHom J) = f

decls.name: Bialgebra.Quotient.liftBialgHom_unique
decls.doc:
A bialgebra morphism out of the quotient is determined by its precomposition with the
quotient map.
decls.statement:
theorem liftBialgHom_unique (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : J ≤ RingHom.ker f.toAlgHom.toRingHom) (g : H ⧸ J →ₐc[R] K)
    (hg : g.comp (Bialgebra.Quotient.mkBialgHom J) = f) :
    g = liftBialgHom J f hf

decls.name: TauCeti.Bialgebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
decls.doc:
The left inclusion `x ↦ x ⊗ₜ 1` of a bialgebra into a tensor product of bialgebras,
packaged as a bialgebra morphism. It is the unit `R →ₐc[R] H₂` tensored on the right with `H₁`,
precomposed with the right-unit isomorphism `H₁ ≃ₐc[R] H₁ ⊗[R] R`.
decls.statement: def includeLeft : H₁ →ₐc[R] H₁ ⊗[R] H₂

decls.name: TauCeti.Bialgebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
decls.doc:
The right inclusion `y ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ y` of a bialgebra into a tensor product of bialgebras,
packaged as a bialgebra morphism. It is the unit `R →ₐc[R] H₁` tensored on the left with `H₂`,
precomposed with the left-unit isomorphism `H₂ ≃ₐc[R] R ⊗[R] H₂`.
decls.statement: def includeRight : H₂ →ₐc[R] H₁ ⊗[R] H₂

decls.name: TauCeti.Bialgebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft_apply
decls.statement: theorem includeLeft_apply (x : H₁) : includeLeft (H₂ := H₂) x = x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : H₂)

decls.name: TauCeti.Bialgebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_apply
decls.statement: theorem includeRight_apply (y : H₂) : includeRight (H₁ := H₁) y = (1 : H₁) ⊗ₜ[R] y

decls.name: TauCeti.Bialgebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft_toAlgHom
decls.statement:
theorem includeLeft_toAlgHom :
    (includeLeft : H₁ →ₐc[R] H₁ ⊗[R] H₂).toAlgHom = Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft

decls.name: TauCeti.Bialgebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_toAlgHom
decls.statement:
theorem includeRight_toAlgHom :
    (includeRight : H₂ →ₐc[R] H₁ ⊗[R] H₂).toAlgHom = Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight

decls.name: TauCeti.CommAlgCat.restrictScalarsObj
decls.doc: Restrict a commutative `K`-algebra to a commutative `k`-algebra along `f : k →+* K`.
decls.statement:
abbrev restrictScalarsObj (f : k →+* K) (A : _root_.CommAlgCat.{x} K) :
    _root_.CommAlgCat.{x} k

decls.name: TauCeti.CommAlgCat.algebraMap_restrictScalarsObj
decls.doc: The restricted `k`-algebra structure has scalar map `algebraMap K A ∘ f`.
decls.statement:
lemma algebraMap_restrictScalarsObj (f : k →+* K) (A : _root_.CommAlgCat.{x} K) (r : k) :
    algebraMap k (restrictScalarsObj f A) r = algebraMap K A (f r)

decls.name: TauCeti.CommAlgCat.restrictScalarsMap
decls.doc:
Restrict a morphism of commutative `K`-algebras to a morphism of commutative
`k`-algebras along `f : k →+* K`.

decls.name: TauCeti.CommAlgCat.restrictScalarsMap_hom
decls.doc:
The underlying algebra hom of a restricted categorical morphism is restriction of scalars
on the original algebra hom.
decls.statement:
lemma restrictScalarsMap_hom {A B : _root_.CommAlgCat.{x} K}
    (f : k →+* K) (χ : A ⟶ B) :
    (restrictScalarsMap f χ).hom =
      letI : Algebra k K

decls.name: TauCeti.CommAlgCat.restrictScalars
decls.doc: The restriction-of-scalars functor `CommAlgCat K ⥤ CommAlgCat k` along `f : k →+* K`.
decls.statement:
abbrev restrictScalars (f : k →+* K) :
    _root_.CommAlgCat.{x} K ⥤ _root_.CommAlgCat.{x} k

decls.name: TauCeti.CommAlgCat.restrictScalars_obj
decls.doc: The object part of `restrictScalars` is restriction of scalars on algebras.
decls.statement:
lemma restrictScalars_obj (f : k →+* K) (A : _root_.CommAlgCat.{x} K) :
    (restrictScalars f).obj A = restrictScalarsObj f A

decls.name: TauCeti.CommAlgCat.restrictScalars_map
decls.doc: The morphism part of `restrictScalars` is restriction of scalars on morphisms.
decls.statement:
lemma restrictScalars_map (f : k →+* K) {A B : _root_.CommAlgCat.{x} K} (χ : A ⟶ B) :
    (restrictScalars f).map χ = restrictScalarsMap f χ

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible
decls.doc:
Local generators exhibit a sheaf of modules as invertible when they freely generate it
on a cover and every local generating type has exactly one element.
decls.statement: structure LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible (q : SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData M) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
decls.doc:
A sheaf of modules is invertible if it is locally free of rank one. The witness is
local generator data whose free presentations are isomorphisms and whose basis types have
exactly one element.
decls.statement: class IsInvertible : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible.isLocallyFree
decls.doc: An invertible sheaf is locally free.
decls.statement:
instance IsInvertible.isLocallyFree (M : SheafOfModules.{u} R) [h : IsInvertible M] :
    M.IsLocallyFree

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.ofIso
decls.doc:
Transport local generator data along an isomorphism of sheaves of modules: the same cover, with
each family of local generators pushed forward along the restricted isomorphism.
decls.statement:
def LocalGeneratorsData.ofIso (q : SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData M) (e : M ≅ N) :
    SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData N

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible.ofIso
decls.doc: Rank-one local generator data stays rank one after transport along an isomorphism.

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible.of_iso
decls.doc: Invertibility transports along an isomorphism of sheaves of modules.
decls.statement: theorem IsInvertible.of_iso (e : M ≅ N) [h : IsInvertible M] : IsInvertible N

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.free_isInvertible
decls.doc: A free sheaf whose indexing type has exactly one element is an invertible sheaf.
decls.statement:
instance free_isInvertible (I : Type u) [Nonempty I] [Subsingleton I] :
    IsInvertible (SheafOfModules.free (R := R) I)

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalTrivializations
decls.doc:
A local trivialization atlas for a sheaf of modules. It consists of a cover of the terminal
object and, over every member of the cover, an isomorphism from the standard free rank-one
sheaf to the restriction of `M`.
decls.statement: structure LocalTrivializations (M : SheafOfModules.{u} R)

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible.trivializationIso
decls.doc:
A rank-one free presentation on a member of a cover, standardized to an isomorphism from
the free sheaf on `PUnit`.

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible.trivializationIso_hom
decls.doc:
The forward map of the standardized trivialization is the relabelling of the free basis,
followed by the original local free presentation.
decls.statement:
lemma trivializationIso_hom {q : SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData M}
    (hq : LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible q) (i : q.I) :
    (hq.trivializationIso i).hom =
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.freeFunctor (R := R.over (q.X i))).map
        (@Equiv.punitOfNonemptyOfSubsingleton (q.generators i).I
          (hq.basisNonempty i) (hq.basisSubsingleton i)).symm.toIso.hom ≫
        (q.generators i).π

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalTrivializations.ofIso
decls.doc: Transport local trivializations along an isomorphism of sheaves of modules.
decls.statement: def ofIso (t : LocalTrivializations M) (e : M ≅ N) : LocalTrivializations N

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalTrivializations.ofIso_I
decls.doc: Transporting local trivializations preserves the indexing type.
decls.statement:
lemma ofIso_I (t : LocalTrivializations M) (e : M ≅ N) :
    (t.ofIso e).I = t.I

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalTrivializations.ofIso_X
decls.doc: Transporting local trivializations preserves the covering objects.
decls.statement:
lemma ofIso_X (t : LocalTrivializations M) (e : M ≅ N) :
    (t.ofIso e).X = fun i ↦ t.X ((ofIso_I t e).mp i)

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalTrivializations.ofIso_iso
decls.doc: The transported trivializations are obtained by composing with the restricted isomorphism.
decls.statement:
lemma ofIso_iso (t : LocalTrivializations M) (e : M ≅ N) (i : (t.ofIso e).I) :
    (t.ofIso e).iso i =
      cast (by rw [ofIso_X])
        (t.iso ((ofIso_I t e).mp i) ≪≫
          (SheafOfModules.overFunctor R (t.X ((ofIso_I t e).mp i))).mapIso e)

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalTrivializations.isInvertible
decls.doc: Local trivializations exhibit a sheaf as invertible.
decls.statement: theorem isInvertible (t : LocalTrivializations M) : IsInvertible M

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalTrivializations.ofIsInvertible
decls.doc: Every invertible sheaf admits local trivializations by the standard free rank-one sheaf.
decls.statement:
def ofIsInvertible (M : SheafOfModules.{u} R) [hM : IsInvertible M] :
    LocalTrivializations M

decls.name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.LocalTrivializations.nonempty_iff_isInvertible
decls.doc:
A sheaf of modules is invertible exactly when it admits a local trivialization atlas by
the standard free rank-one sheaf.
decls.statement:
theorem nonempty_iff_isInvertible :
    Nonempty (LocalTrivializations M) ↔ IsInvertible M

decls.name: TauCeti.isCentral_of_isCentral_matrix
decls.doc:
If a matrix algebra `Matrix ι ι D` over a nonempty finite index type is central over `K`, then
its coefficient algebra `D` is central over `K`.

The centre of `Matrix ι ι D` is the image of the centre of `D` under the scalar embedding
`Matrix.scalarAlgHom`, which is injective because `ι` is nonempty; so the centre of `D` is `⊥` as
soon as the centre of the matrix algebra is. This is the converse of `Algebra.IsCentral.matrix`.
decls.statement:
theorem isCentral_of_isCentral_matrix [Algebra.IsCentral K (Matrix ι ι D)] :
    Algebra.IsCentral K D

decls.name: TauCeti.isCentral_matrix_iff
decls.doc:
A matrix algebra over a nonempty finite index type is central exactly when its coefficient
algebra is.
decls.statement:
theorem isCentral_matrix_iff :
    Algebra.IsCentral K (Matrix ι ι D) ↔ Algebra.IsCentral K D

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSimpleRing.exists_algEquiv_matrix_centralDivisionRing
decls.doc:
**Wedderburn-Artin for central simple algebras.** A finite-dimensional central simple
`K`-algebra `A` is isomorphic to a matrix algebra over a finite-dimensional **central** division
`K`-algebra `D`, and then `finrank K A = n ^ 2 * finrank K D`.

Mathlib's `IsSimpleRing.exists_algEquiv_matrix_divisionRing_finite` supplies everything except the
centrality of `D`, which comes from `TauCeti.isCentral_of_isCentral_matrix`.
decls.title: Wedderburn-Artin for central simple algebras
decls.statement:
theorem exists_algEquiv_matrix_centralDivisionRing [Algebra.IsCentral K A] [IsSimpleRing A]
    [FiniteDimensional K A] :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : NeZero n) (D : Type u) (_ : DivisionRing D) (_ : Algebra K D)
      (_ : Algebra.IsCentral K D) (_ : FiniteDimensional K D),
      Module.finrank K A = n ^ 2 * Module.finrank K D ∧
        Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[K] Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) D)

decls.name: TauCeti.baseFieldAlgEquivOfFinite
decls.doc:
A **finite central division algebra over a field is the base field**, as an isomorphism of
`K`-algebras.

A finite division ring is a field by little Wedderburn (the instance `littleWedderburn`), so `K → D`
is a central extension of fields and `Algebra.IsCentral.baseField_essentially_unique` applied to the
tower `D / D / K` makes it bijective. Centrality is essential: `𝔽_{q^m}` is a finite division
algebra over `𝔽_q` whose structure map is not surjective for `m > 1`.
decls.statement: def baseFieldAlgEquivOfFinite : D ≃ₐ[K] K

decls.name: TauCeti.baseFieldAlgEquivOfFinite_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem baseFieldAlgEquivOfFinite_symm_apply (a : K) :
    (baseFieldAlgEquivOfFinite K D).symm a = algebraMap K D a

decls.name: TauCeti.algebraMap_baseFieldAlgEquivOfFinite
decls.statement:
theorem algebraMap_baseFieldAlgEquivOfFinite (x : D) :
    algebraMap K D (baseFieldAlgEquivOfFinite K D x) = x

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_eq_one_of_finite
decls.doc: A finite central division algebra over a field is one-dimensional over it.
decls.statement: theorem finrank_eq_one_of_finite : Module.finrank K D = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSimpleRing.exists_algEquiv_matrix_of_finite
decls.doc:
**A central simple algebra over a finite field is a full matrix algebra.** Over a finite field
the only finite-dimensional central division algebra is the field itself, so the division algebra in
the Wedderburn presentation collapses and `finrank K A = n ^ 2`.

This is the finite-field analogue of Mathlib's
`IsSimpleRing.exists_algEquiv_matrix_of_isAlgClosed`; note that `IsSimpleRing A` alone would not
suffice, since `A` could be a proper field extension of `K`.
decls.title: A central simple algebra over a finite field is a full matrix algebra
decls.statement:
theorem exists_algEquiv_matrix_of_finite :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : NeZero n), Module.finrank K A = n ^ 2 ∧
      Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[K] Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSimpleRing.isSquare_finrank_of_finite
decls.doc: The dimension of a central simple algebra over a finite field is a perfect square.
decls.statement: theorem isSquare_finrank_of_finite : IsSquare (Module.finrank K A)

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule
decls.doc:
A right comodule over an `R`-coalgebra `C`.

The coaction is written as a linear map `coact : M →ₗ[R] M ⊗[R] C`. The coassociativity law
says that coacting twice on the `M` component agrees with coacting once and then
comultiplying the `C` component. The counit law says that applying the coalgebra counit to
the `C` component recovers the original vector, under the canonical `M ⊗ R` presentation.
decls.statement:
class Comodule (R : Type u) (C : Type v) (M : Type w) [CommSemiring R]
    [AddCommMonoid C] [Module R C] [Coalgebra R C] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.coact_coassoc
decls.doc: Coassociativity of the coaction, as an equality of linear maps.
decls.statement:
theorem coact_coassoc :
    TensorProduct.assoc R M C C ∘ₗ (coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := M)).rTensor C ∘ₗ
        coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := M) =
      Coalgebra.comul.lTensor M ∘ₗ coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := M)

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.coassoc_apply
decls.doc: Coassociativity of the coaction, evaluated at a vector.
decls.statement:
theorem coassoc_apply (m : M) :
    TensorProduct.assoc R M C C
        ((coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := M)).rTensor C (coact m)) =
      Coalgebra.comul.lTensor M (coact m)

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.lTensor_counit_coact
decls.doc: The counit law of the coaction, evaluated at a vector.
decls.statement:
theorem lTensor_counit_coact (m : M) :
    Coalgebra.counit.lTensor M (coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := M) m) = m ⊗ₜ[R] 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.instSelf
decls.doc:
The regular right comodule of a coalgebra over itself, with coaction given by the
coalgebra comultiplication.
decls.statement: instance instSelf : Comodule R C C

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.instSelf_coact
decls.doc: The coaction of the regular right comodule is the coalgebra comultiplication.
decls.statement:
theorem instSelf_coact :
    coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := C) = Coalgebra.comul

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom
decls.doc: A morphism of right comodules over a fixed coalgebra.
decls.statement:
structure Hom (R : Type u) (C : Type v) (M : Type w) (N : Type x) [CommSemiring R]
    [AddCommMonoid C] [Module R C] [Coalgebra R C] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    [Comodule R C M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [Comodule R C N]
    extends M →ₗ[R] N

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.funLike
decls.statement: instance funLike : FunLike (Hom R C M N) M N

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.Simps.apply
decls.doc: See Note [custom simps projection].
decls.statement: def Simps.apply (f : Hom R C M N) : M → N

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.coe_mk
decls.statement: theorem coe_mk {f : M →ₗ[R] N} (h) : ((⟨f, h⟩ : Hom R C M N) : M → N) = f

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.coe_toLinearMap
decls.statement: theorem coe_toLinearMap (f : Hom R C M N) : ⇑f.toLinearMap = f

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.ext
decls.doc: Two comodule morphisms are equal when their underlying functions are equal.
decls.statement: theorem ext {f g : Hom R C M N} (h : ∀ m, f m = g m) : f = g

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.map_coact_eq
decls.doc: A comodule morphism commutes with coactions, as an equality of linear maps.
decls.statement:
theorem map_coact_eq (f : Hom R C M N) :
    TensorProduct.map f.toLinearMap LinearMap.id ∘ₗ coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := M) =
      coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := N) ∘ₗ f.toLinearMap

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.map_coact_apply
decls.doc: A comodule morphism commutes with coactions, evaluated at a vector.
decls.statement:
theorem map_coact_apply (f : Hom R C M N) (m : M) :
    TensorProduct.map f.toLinearMap LinearMap.id (coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := M) m) =
      coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := N) (f m)

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.id
decls.doc: The identity morphism of a right comodule.
decls.statement: def id : Hom R C M M

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.comp
decls.doc: Composition of right-comodule morphisms.
decls.statement: def comp (g : Hom R C N P) (f : Hom R C M N) : Hom R C M P

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.id_toLinearMap
decls.doc: The underlying linear map of the identity morphism is the identity linear map.
decls.statement: theorem id_toLinearMap : (id R C M).toLinearMap = LinearMap.id

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.comp_toLinearMap
decls.doc:
The underlying linear map of a composition is the composition of the underlying linear
maps.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_toLinearMap (g : Hom R C N P) (f : Hom R C M N) :
    (g.comp f).toLinearMap = g.toLinearMap ∘ₗ f.toLinearMap

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.id_comp
decls.statement: theorem id_comp (f : Hom R C M N) : comp (id R C N) f = f

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.comp_id
decls.statement: theorem comp_id (f : Hom R C M N) : comp f (id R C M) = f

decls.name: TauCeti.Comodule.Hom.comp_assoc
decls.statement:
theorem comp_assoc (h : Hom R C P Q) (g : Hom R C N P) (f : Hom R C M N) :
    comp (comp h g) f = comp h (comp g f)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat
decls.doc: The category of right comodules over a fixed `R`-coalgebra `C`.
decls.statement: structure ComoduleCat extends SemimoduleCat.{w} R

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.instCoeSortType
decls.statement: instance : CoeSort (ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C) (Type w)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.instAddCommMonoidCarrier
decls.statement: instance (M : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C) : AddCommMonoid M

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.instModuleCarrier
decls.statement: instance (M : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C) : Module R M

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.of
decls.doc: Build a bundled comodule from a type carrying the usual unbundled typeclasses.
decls.statement:
abbrev of (M : Type w) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Comodule R C M] :
    ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.of_coact
decls.doc: The coaction on `ComoduleCat.of` is the original unbundled coaction.
decls.statement:
theorem of_coact {M : Type w} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Comodule R C M] :
    Comodule.coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := of R C M) =
      Comodule.coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := M)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.Hom
decls.doc: Morphisms in `ComoduleCat` are morphisms of the underlying right comodules.
decls.statement: abbrev Hom (M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.category
decls.statement: instance category : Category (ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.homZero
decls.doc: The zero structure on categorical morphisms is the zero comodule morphism.
decls.statement: instance homZero (M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C) : Zero (M ⟶ N)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.homAdd
decls.doc: Addition of categorical morphisms is pointwise addition of comodule morphisms.
decls.statement: instance homAdd (M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C) : Add (M ⟶ N)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.homAddCommMonoid
decls.doc: Categorical morphisms form an additive commutative monoid under pointwise operations.
decls.statement: instance homAddCommMonoid (M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C) : AddCommMonoid (M ⟶ N)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.homSMul
decls.doc:
Scalar multiplication of categorical morphisms is pointwise scalar multiplication of
comodule morphisms.
decls.statement: instance homSMul (M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C) : SMul R (M ⟶ N)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.homModule
decls.doc: Categorical morphisms form an `R`-module under pointwise operations.
decls.statement: instance homModule (M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C) : Module R (M ⟶ N)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.concreteCategory
decls.doc: `ComoduleCat` is concrete, with concrete morphisms the bundled comodule morphisms.
decls.statement:
instance concreteCategory :
    ConcreteCategory (ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C)
      (fun M N => Comodule.Hom R C M N)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.hom
decls.doc: Turn a morphism in `ComoduleCat` back into its underlying comodule morphism.
decls.statement:
abbrev hom {M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (f : M ⟶ N) :
    Comodule.Hom R C M N

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.ofHom
decls.doc: Typecheck an unbundled comodule morphism as a morphism in `ComoduleCat`.
decls.statement:
abbrev ofHom {M N : Type w} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Comodule R C M]
    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [Comodule R C N] (f : Comodule.Hom R C M N) :
    of R C M ⟶ of R C N

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.hom_ofHom
decls.doc: Turning an unbundled comodule morphism into a categorical morphism and back is the identity.
decls.statement:
theorem hom_ofHom {M N : Type w} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Comodule R C M]
    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [Comodule R C N] (f : Comodule.Hom R C M N) :
    ConcreteCategory.hom (C := ComoduleCat R C) (ofHom (R := R) (C := C) f) = f

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.ofHom_hom
decls.doc: Turning a categorical morphism into an unbundled comodule morphism and back is the identity.
decls.statement:
theorem ofHom_hom {M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (f : M ⟶ N) :
    ofHom (R := R) (C := C) (ConcreteCategory.hom (C := ComoduleCat R C) f) = f

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.ofHom_id
decls.doc: The categorical identity is the bundled form of the identity comodule morphism.
decls.statement:
theorem ofHom_id {M : Type w} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Comodule R C M] :
    ofHom (R := R) (C := C) (Comodule.Hom.id R C M) = 𝟙 (of R C M)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.ofHom_comp
decls.doc: Categorical composition is the bundled form of composition of comodule morphisms.
decls.statement:
theorem ofHom_comp {M N P : Type w} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Comodule R C M]
    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [Comodule R C N]
    [AddCommMonoid P] [Module R P] [Comodule R C P] (f : Comodule.Hom R C M N)
    (g : Comodule.Hom R C N P) :
    ofHom (R := R) (C := C) (Comodule.Hom.comp g f) =
      ofHom (R := R) (C := C) f ≫ ofHom (R := R) (C := C) g

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.ofHom_apply
decls.doc: The bundled form of a comodule morphism applies as the original morphism.
decls.statement:
theorem ofHom_apply {M N : Type w} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Comodule R C M]
    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [Comodule R C N] (f : Comodule.Hom R C M N) (m : M) :
    ofHom (R := R) (C := C) f m = f m

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.homLinearMap
decls.doc: The underlying linear map of a `ComoduleCat` morphism.
decls.statement: abbrev homLinearMap {M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (f : M ⟶ N) : M →ₗ[R] N

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.hom_ext
decls.doc: Two morphisms of bundled comodules are equal when their underlying functions are equal.
decls.statement:
theorem hom_ext {M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} {f g : M ⟶ N}
    (h : ∀ m, f m = g m) : f = g

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.toLinearMap_id
decls.doc: The identity morphism has the identity linear map underneath.
decls.statement:
theorem toLinearMap_id (M : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C) :
    (𝟙 M : M ⟶ M).toLinearMap = LinearMap.id

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.toLinearMap_comp
decls.doc: Composition in `ComoduleCat` is composition of the underlying linear maps.
decls.statement:
theorem toLinearMap_comp {M N P : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (f : M ⟶ N) (g : N ⟶ P) :
    (f ≫ g).toLinearMap = g.toLinearMap.comp f.toLinearMap

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.id_apply
decls.doc: The identity morphism acts as the identity function.
decls.statement:
theorem id_apply (M : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C) (m : M) :
    (𝟙 M : M ⟶ M) m = m

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.comp_apply
decls.doc: Composition of morphisms acts by ordinary function composition.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_apply {M N P : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (f : M ⟶ N) (g : N ⟶ P)
    (m : M) :
    (f ≫ g) m = g (f m)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.toLinearMap_zero
decls.doc: The zero morphism has the zero linear map underneath.
decls.statement:
theorem toLinearMap_zero (M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C) :
    (0 : M ⟶ N).toLinearMap = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.toLinearMap_add
decls.doc: Addition of morphisms is addition of the underlying linear maps.
decls.statement:
theorem toLinearMap_add {M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (f g : M ⟶ N) :
    (f + g).toLinearMap = f.toLinearMap + g.toLinearMap

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.toLinearMap_nsmul
decls.doc:
Natural-number scalar multiplication of morphisms is natural-number scalar multiplication
of the underlying linear maps.
decls.statement:
theorem toLinearMap_nsmul {M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (n : ℕ) (f : M ⟶ N) :
    (n • f).toLinearMap = n • f.toLinearMap

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.toLinearMap_smul
decls.doc: Scalar multiplication of morphisms is scalar multiplication of the underlying linear maps.
decls.statement:
theorem toLinearMap_smul {M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (r : R) (f : M ⟶ N) :
    (r • f).toLinearMap = r • f.toLinearMap

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.toLinearMap_sum
decls.doc: Finite sums of morphisms are finite sums of the underlying linear maps.
decls.statement:
theorem toLinearMap_sum {ι : Type*} {M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (s : Finset ι)
    (f : ι → (M ⟶ N)) :
    (∑ i ∈ s, f i).toLinearMap = ∑ i ∈ s, (f i).toLinearMap

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.zero_apply
decls.doc: The zero morphism acts as the zero function.
decls.statement:
theorem zero_apply {M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (m : M) :
    (0 : M ⟶ N) m = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.add_apply
decls.doc: Addition of morphisms acts by pointwise addition.
decls.statement:
theorem add_apply {M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (f g : M ⟶ N) (m : M) :
    (f + g) m = f m + g m

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.nsmul_apply
decls.doc:
Natural-number scalar multiplication of morphisms acts by pointwise natural-number scalar
multiplication.
decls.statement:
theorem nsmul_apply {M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (n : ℕ) (f : M ⟶ N) (m : M) :
    (n • f) m = n • f m

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.smul_apply
decls.doc: Scalar multiplication of morphisms acts by pointwise scalar multiplication.
decls.statement:
theorem smul_apply {M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (r : R) (f : M ⟶ N) (m : M) :
    (r • f) m = r • f m

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.sum_apply
decls.doc: Finite sums of morphisms act by pointwise finite sums.
decls.statement:
theorem sum_apply {ι : Type*} {M N : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (s : Finset ι)
    (f : ι → (M ⟶ N)) (m : M) :
    (∑ i ∈ s, f i) m = ∑ i ∈ s, f i m

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.add_comp
decls.doc: Composition in `ComoduleCat` is additive in the left morphism.
decls.statement:
theorem add_comp {M N P : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (f g : M ⟶ N) (h : N ⟶ P) :
    (f + g) ≫ h = f ≫ h + g ≫ h

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.comp_add
decls.doc: Composition in `ComoduleCat` is additive in the right morphism.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_add {M N P : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (f : M ⟶ N) (g h : N ⟶ P) :
    f ≫ (g + h) = f ≫ g + f ≫ h

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.smul_comp
decls.doc:
Composition in `ComoduleCat` is compatible with scalar multiplication in the left
morphism.
decls.statement:
theorem smul_comp {M N P : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (r : R) (f : M ⟶ N) (g : N ⟶ P) :
    (r • f) ≫ g = r • (f ≫ g)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.comp_smul
decls.doc:
Composition in `ComoduleCat` is compatible with scalar multiplication in the right
morphism.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_smul {M N P : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (r : R) (f : M ⟶ N) (g : N ⟶ P) :
    f ≫ (r • g) = r • (f ≫ g)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.zero_comp
decls.doc: Composing the zero morphism on the left gives the zero morphism.
decls.statement:
theorem zero_comp {M N P : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (f : N ⟶ P) :
    (0 : M ⟶ N) ≫ f = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.comp_zero
decls.doc: Composing the zero morphism on the right gives the zero morphism.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_zero {M N P : ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C} (f : M ⟶ N) :
    f ≫ (0 : N ⟶ P) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.hasZeroMorphisms
decls.doc: `ComoduleCat` has the standard categorical zero morphisms.
decls.statement:
instance hasZeroMorphisms :
    CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms (ComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C)

decls.name: TauCeti.ComoduleCat.hasForgetToSemimodule
